Many people get to work flexible schedules in exchange for working late/off hours. Instead of having that be an opaque deal that makes people feel stressed and abused, we need to embrace that reality and come up with a written policy that explains this reality.

For my part, just because I work on an urgent issue from 9PM-12AM, or have to work during my PTO, I don't feel like I can "safely" take some extra time to myself the next day, or cut out early on Friday. The calls and emails don't stop, so it becomes basically impossible to disengage. I know that anyone who I explain it to will be understanding, but it still doesn't feel right.

Bring it out in to the open with a "DWS Dependability Promise", e.g.: Our work is 24/7/365, and we need to be there to support the field operation and our own teams whenever we are needed. However, all DWS employees are expected to maintain a healthy balance in order to protect themselves and the company. As a full time salary employee, any exempt and approved overtime beyond 10 hours per pay period may be offset with personal time taken during business hours in the same pay period.

item:43: Smaller meeting sizes.  It seems every meeting has too many participants which often hinders progress due to the "too many cooks in the kitchen" effect, where excessive input can lead to confusion and dilute decision-making clarity. When numerous individuals contribute, it becomes challenging to maintain a focused agenda and arrive at clear, actionable decisions. The diversity of opinions, while valuable, can result in prolonged discussions and conflicting viewpoints, which often delay consensus.  This dynamic can extend meeting times unnecessarily and complicate the path to a decisive and effective resolution, ultimately slowing down project momentum and efficiency.   This same effect happens when everyone cc's everyone and hits reply all to every email chain.  It's become apparent that "cc:" is now synonymous with "To:" Perhaps this is a result of our growth and we've become unsure of who is responsible for what, but emails fly everywhere and to everyone.  I would like to see some training on email etiquette and when you should hit "reply all".

Making the hands sit at the hotel while the rig is in the shop is terrible for moral. Although I understand the reasoning. item:43: I went from one rig where the roughnecks were switching out to other rigs on a regular basis to a rig where they were steady. It was night and day. Why was it like that on the last rig and not on this one? Who knows. If my weakest team members are a revolving door it’s impossible for me to keep the worksite safe. The bottom 3 guys should stay with a rig/supervisor until they are lead hand 2 or operators. They need a stable mentor and a supervisor needs people he can rely on and hold accountable. Losing hands multiple times a hitch to another rig or not being able to get rid of hands you want to is crippling the safety at this company. If I want to remove an employee from my team it shouldn’t be a battle. They may fit somewhere else that is great, we shouldn’t be required to write someone up to remove them from our unit. Often multiple write ups are the only way. I can’t write someone up because they don’t share the correct core values that make a crew thrive for example. Concentrating 100% of your bandwidth on keeping the inexperienced employees safe means you have no bandwidth left to prevent incidents at the upper levels. On a side note, optimal schedule would have the bottom 3 paired with a supervisor for 28 days so he can mentor them, operator for 14 days so they can get time learning from multiple supervisors before they progress and perhaps a lead hand for 21 days. I think this would allow us to train and mentor our guys to the level we need much quicker and obtain the organic growth we are looking for at this massive rate of expansion. Safety meetings for example. If I have 3 guys who understand how to write it correctly I don’t need to train a new hire every other week and spend 15 minutes after the meeting correcting it or re teaching them. Time I should be using going over the equipment and ensuring the crew is coming on tower safely.

I do think communication could be better between the different departments.   However one thing that I think could easily help at least the tong area.   Is to have the redtag filled out stating the known mechanical issues with tongs.  I know we all have gotten away from using them at times, myself included.     However, someone in the field had been running the tongs.  Someone knows at least a few issues that are wrong.  A lot of time is wasted on our side, trying to investigate the issues, if any at all.   We need to replace certain pieces each time they are used.  So if certain pieces of equipment are going out and being completely unused while on pad.  Those items that need to be replaced each time, would not need replaced in that situation. 

For example. We change backing stop bolts on Universe tongs each time they are used in field.  It takes roughly 2 hours to completely dismantle the necessary pieces and replace the bolts. Rebuilding tongs. If they were just rebuilt and replaced on 9/21 and the tongs came back in on 9/28.  If one of the two set on the skid are unused or both are unused but rusty. Shop time is investing in the employees. Right now it feels like the hands are literally just resource equipment that just gets stacked out when they’re not turning a profit. The knowledge level of tongs and slips etc in these new lead hands is pathetic. But it’s not because they’re in not able to learn. I feel they’re being robbed of not only fair wages but also the chance to grow in their positions. How are they gonna learn to fix the tongs when the situation require us to stay billable when they haven’t been given the chance to leisurely take them apart and learn them in a relaxed environment. When I was a lead hand and operator my supervisor never had to come to the basket to fix things on a job because we were competent enough to do it efficiently ourselves. There wasn’t a competency program, we just were aloud, actually REQUIRED to come to the shop every day and invest our time and learn the necessary knowledge to do our job to the fullest.
